_doc: The weekly scout report: what exists out there that this box is not using. Written by the Claude routine described in docs/models.md and read by src/lib/model-scout.ts. Judgment lives here; facts about which model ids a vendor currently sells are NOT — those are pulled live from each vendor's model-list endpoint at read time, because a list committed to git is out of date the day after it is written. Fit verdicts are likewise computed at read time and never stored here: a verdict depends on what is running and how much disk is free, and both change hourly. They are now computed PER HOST — measured against the machine this console is running on, and against each other host's declared specs in config/hosts/*.json — so a claim in `why` or `notes` that a model does not fit needs to name which machine it means.
_schema: candidates[]: { id, name, kind: local|cloud, capability, why, checkpoint?, provider?, target?, mode?, params?, released?, license?, docs?, paper?, requirement? { vramGb, ramGb, diskGb, basis, estimated }, spec? { paramsB, precision, contextK, kind }, runtimes?, pricing? }. Give `requirement` when the authors published usable numbers; give `spec` otherwise and let estimateFromParams() do the arithmetic with an honest basis string. `runtimes` pins weights to one stack (e.g. ["metal"] for an MLX repo) and MUST be omitted for portable weights, which is most of them — absent means "runs anywhere", and GGUF counts as portable. Verdicts are computed per HOST: name which machine you mean in `why` and `notes`, because BeTenshi (31.8 GB VRAM + 63 GB host RAM) and B5 (one 128 GB unified pool) disagree about a good number of models. upgrades[]: { alias, from, to, why } — a like-for-like repoint of an alias already in ai-router.yaml.
generatedBy: weekly scout, 2026-10-05 — the week the speech-to-text case got re-proved mechanically and the cloud half moved under last week's feet. The Open ASR Leaderboard's 02-10-2026 build was pulled whole and cross-joined: of 52 open models on the short-form English board, exactly four also appear on the long-form and multilingual boards, and exactly one of those four beats the whisper-large-v3 that BeTenshi still serves on :8001 on all three. Meanwhile Anthropic shipped claude-opus-5-5 (22-09) and claude-sonnet-5-5 (28-09) AFTER the last run, so two of this file's five standing repoints were aiming at models that are themselves now superseded. Against that, the Open TTS Leaderboard's results dataset has gone private, which costs this report the ability to re-verify its own TTS numbers — said plainly below rather than papered over.

candidates.name: Cohere Transcribe (03-2026)
candidates.license: apache-2.0 (repo is gated: auto — click-through; re-checked 05-10 against the hub API, still `auto`, not `manual`)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 05-10 and byte-for-byte unchanged for the seventh week: model.safetensors 4,131,862,976 B plus config, tokenizer, two card images and a demo wav = 4,134,794,009 B for the whole repo. Against the 2,065,804,048 params HF reports that file is exactly 2 bytes/param, so it is a plain bf16 release with no codec or encoder outside the count. VRAM is the weights at bf16 (4.13 GB) x 1.15 runtime overhead; ASR has no KV cache worth budgeting at 30-second chunks. Estimated, because Cohere publishes no memory figure.

candidates.why: THE PICK, FOR BETENSHI, and the single thing on this list most worth doing this week — now 42 days outstanding, dated from `git log --follow config/model-scout.json` (first raised 2026-08-24), not counted by hand. BeTenshi still serves stt from whisper-large-v3 on :8001. On the Open ASR Leaderboard build dated 02-10-2026 that model is open #35 of 52 on short-form English. This week the claim behind this entry was re-proved mechanically rather than re-asserted: the three boards were pulled as CSVs and joined on model id. Only FOUR open models appear on all three — this one, nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3, whisper-large-v3 and whisper-large-v3-turbo — and only this one beats whisper-large-v3 on every one: short-form English 4.67 vs 5.78 (19% relative), long-form 9.73 vs 11.23 (13%), multilingual 3.83 vs 4.81 (20%). It is also 2.4x the throughput (RTFx 906.6 vs 470.2) and 4.13 GB on disk against a 1.5B int8 service. The cost is languages: 14 declared against whisper's 99, and Arabic IS among them, which is the one this box actually cares about. THIS IS A BETENSHI RECOMMENDATION AND NOT A B5 ONE: B5 already serves qwen3-asr-1.7b-8bit through MLX-Audio, and against that Cohere is a trade rather than a win — it loses short-form English 4.67 vs 4.31 and wins multilingual 3.83 vs 5.11, with Qwen3-ASR unmeasured on long-form. On size, 4.8 GB is unremarkable on either machine: it fits beside everything on BeTenshi's 31.8 GB card and is noise in B5's 128 GB pool.

candidates.name: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, read 05-10: the repo ships the SAME checkpoint in three formats — model.safetensors 2,508,311,120 B, parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3.nemo 2,509,332,480 B and parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3.q8_0.gguf 713,975,456 B — so a plain `hf download` costs 5,732,941,955 B for the whole repo while only one format is ever loaded. diskGb is the whole-repo figure deliberately, because that is what the download actually costs; an --include '*.safetensors' pull is 2.51 GB and the q8_0 GGUF alone is 0.71 GB. 2,508,311,120 B against the 627,077,780 params HF reports is exactly 4 bytes/param, so the safetensors release is fp32, not bf16 — worth saying, because it means the obvious memory estimate from the parameter count is half the real one. VRAM is the fp32 weights (2.51 GB) x 1.15 runtime overhead; a FastConformer encoder has no KV cache to budget. Estimated: NVIDIA publishes no memory figure.

candidates.why: NEW THIS WEEK, AND AN OMISSION THIS REPORT IS CORRECTING IN THE OPEN. This file has been ranking speech-to-text on the Open ASR Leaderboard since 15-09 and never listed the only open model besides Cohere that is measured on all three of its boards. That was a gap, not a judgement, and it is being fixed rather than quietly backfilled. On the 02-10-2026 build it beats BeTenshi's whisper-large-v3 on short-form English (4.859 vs 5.780, 16% relative) and on long-form (10.72 vs 11.23, 4.5%), and is level on multilingual — 4.814 against 4.810 across fourteen language/dataset pairs, a 0.004 gap that is a tie, not a loss, and is reported as a tie here rather than rounded into a win. It is open #16 of 52 on short-form English against Cohere's #10. WHY IT IS NOT THE PICK: Cohere is better on all three boards, and when the question is accuracy that settles it. WHY IT IS HERE ANYWAY, and this is the part neither the leaderboard tab nor a parameter count can say: RTFx 6,076 against whisper's 470 — thirteen times the throughput — 2.9 GB of VRAM against Cohere's 4.8, 25 declared languages, no gate at all, and a q8_0 GGUF of 713,975,456 B sitting in the same repo. That last one matters: it is the only candidate in this lane that can be tried without a Python stack. If the 4.13 GB download or the Cohere click-through is what has kept :8001 on whisper for six weeks, this is the version of the same decision with those obstacles removed. On B5 it is also worth a line, for a different reason: against the installed qwen3-asr-1.7b-8bit it wins multilingual (4.81 vs 5.11) and long-form (10.72 vs unmeasured) and loses short-form English (4.86 vs 4.31). Portable weights, so no `runtimes` pin — it runs on both boxes.

candidates.name: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming 1.5B
candidates.params: 2.81B (the '1.5B' in the name is the LLM backbone only)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 05-10 and byte-for-byte unchanged: model-0000{1,2,3}-of-00003.safetensors 2,498,354,152 + 2,486,576,066 + 643,458,072 B = 5,628,388,290 B of weights, 5,645,212,528 B for the whole repo. Against the 2,814,116,321 params HF reports that is exactly 2 bytes/param, so it is bf16 with no separate codec outside the count. VRAM is the weights (5.63 GB) x 1.15; a streaming decoder holds a small rolling cache, not a full-utterance KV cache. Estimated: Microsoft publishes no memory figure.

candidates.why: 28 days outstanding (first raised 2026-09-07, from git). Its claim is NARROWED AND MADE EXACT this week. Re-checked against the 02-10-2026 build: this checkpoint is still absent from all three boards, so it is UNMEASURED — the 5.575 short-form row under the VibeVoice name belongs to microsoft/VibeVoice-ASR-HF, a different 8B checkpoint, which is the correction the 21-09 run made and which still holds. So this entry does not beat whisper-large-v3 on accuracy and never claimed to; it beats it on a capability whisper does not have at all — neither box can transcribe a live stream today, and :8001 is batch-only. WHAT CHANGED: the board now carries two MEASURED streaming models, nvidia/nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b at 5.245 short-form English (which does beat whisper's 5.780, at RTFx 1,167 and with a 0.70 GB q8_0 GGUF) and nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b at 7.878 across 40 languages. Both are under vendor licences — `nvidia-open-model-license` and `OpenMDW-1.1` — which this report's own licence rule keeps out of `candidates` until a person has read the terms, so they are in `notes` and not here. That leaves this entry with a precise and much smaller claim than it had a month ago: it is the only MIT-licensed streaming ASR with a real release behind it, it is unmeasured, and the measured alternatives are one licence read away from displacing it. On BeTenshi 6.5 GB runs alongside the 7.6 GB Qwen2.5-7B service with room left on the 31.8 GB card; on B5 it is unremarkable.

candidates.name: AuK-Flash (Tencent Hunyuan speech foundation model, distilled)
candidates.params: the Open TTS Leaderboard recorded 1.53B; HF publishes no count and the repo ships 6.76 GB, so the count is still not the footprint

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 05-10 and byte-for-byte unchanged: auk_flash.safetensors 6,122,209,092 B + vae.safetensors 637,322,604 B = 6,759,531,696 B of weights, 6,762,657,045 B for the whole repo. Still byte-for-byte the same size as the AuK base repo, which ships the same VAE beside auk_base.safetensors at the identical 6,122,209,092 B. HF publishes no parameter count for this repo, so the footprint is read off the bytes and not inferred. VRAM is the weights x 1.15, plus headroom for the diffusion sampler. Estimated throughout.

candidates.why: CARRIED, WITH THE SOURCE BEHIND IT NOW BROKEN — and that is said here rather than left for a reader to discover. This entry's whole case is one number: on the Open TTS Leaderboard build dated 18-09-2026, English cloning on CV3-Eval, AuK-Flash scored 72.67 speaker similarity against ResembleAI/chatterbox-multilingual's 53.13 — and Chatterbox is what BeTenshi has been cloning voices with since 18-09 on :8004. A 19-point SIM gap is the kind of margin worth 6.8 GB. THE PROBLEM: that number could not be re-read this week. The board's results dataset, `hf-audio/tts_leaderboard_results`, now returns HTTP 401 anonymously and is not visible to this run's authenticated hub account either, so the CSVs the 21-09 run quoted are no longer public. Worse for this entry specifically, the board's own version registry — still readable in the Space's leaderboard_data.py — shows the current build is 30-09-2026 and labels the 29-09 one 'Sync results programmatically (few instances of bad manual copies from initial version)'. The maintainers are saying some numbers in the build this entry quotes were mis-transcribed. So: the SIM lead is reported here as OF 18-09-2026 AND UNVERIFIED SINCE, not as current. It stays a candidate because the capability argument survives independently of the exact figure — AuK and AuK-Flash were the only two models scored in cloning mode that led Chatterbox on similarity at all — but it must not be adopted on a number this report can no longer open. On BeTenshi 7.8 GB fits beside Kokoro and Chatterbox on the 31.8 GB card; on B5 it is unremarkable, and B5 has no cloning service at all, which makes it the more interesting box for this one if the number ever becomes checkable again.

candidates.name: Qwen3-TTS 12Hz (1.7B CustomVoice)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 05-10 and unchanged: model.safetensors 3,833,402,552 B (= 1,916,676,352 params x 2 bytes, so bf16) PLUS speech_tokenizer/model.safetensors 682,293,092 B, which the 1.7B in the name does not include — 4,520,218,951 B for the whole repo. VRAM is that x 1.15 runtime overhead. Estimated: Qwen publishes no memory figure.

candidates.why: BETENSHI ONLY — B5 has served this through MLX-Audio as `qwen3-tts-1.7b-customvoice` since 20-09, and that has not changed. 42 days outstanding (first raised 2026-08-24). Its case on BeTenshi is breadth and nothing else: the 18-09 board had it third of ten on the all-nine-language CV3-Eval board at 4.22 WER against Chatterbox-multilingual's 11.28, while Kokoro — BeTenshi's default TTS, and second on English at 1.46 — is English-only and is unranked there because it does not cover the nine. So the gap this closes is non-English intelligibility, not quality in English, where it loses to the 82M model already running (1.71 vs 1.46) and is five times slower to first audio (309.9 ms vs 103.9 ms at batch 1). Same caveat as AuK-Flash: those are 18-09 figures and the board's results dataset is no longer readable, so they could not be re-verified this week. THE DOWNLOAD FIGURE IS UPDATED, and which metric is meant is stated as the brief requires. 30-day, read 05-10: this repo 2,366,999, ResembleAI/chatterbox 1,668,253. All-time: this repo 16,229,191, Chatterbox 22,769,265. So Chatterbox leads 1.40x on lifetime and this repo leads 1.42x on the month — the same shape as 18-09, with both monthly figures down (2.61M and 1.86M then). Last week's '2.62M' is now 2.37M; it was a 30-day figure then and is a 30-day figure now, and it has fallen.

upgrades.why: Raised 2026-09-07, so 28 days — four weeks — outstanding, read from `git log --follow config/model-scout.json`. RE-VERIFIED THIS WEEK AGAINST OPENAI'S OWN PUBLISHED PRICING PAGE, not an aggregator, and the 21-09 withdrawal was right and stands: gpt-5.5 IS still carried, at $5.00/$30.00 per 1M input/output, listed with '<272K context length'. gpt-5.6-terra is $2.00/$12.00. So the urgency is cost, not retirement, exactly as last week corrected itself to say. ONE REFINEMENT THIS WEEK, because last week's flat '2.5x cut on both sides' was not the whole rule: terra's $2/$12 applies to inputs at or below 272K tokens and it charges $4/$18 above that. That does not weaken the case, it strengthens it — gpt-5.5 is itself capped below 272K, so the 2.5x cut holds across the entire range gpt-5.5 can serve, and terra additionally buys context gpt-5.5 cannot reach at all. Terra and not sol ($4/$20, $8/$30 long) nor luna ($0.20/$1.20, a different tier of model). All three are already wired under their own ids from the 2026-08-19 sweep, so this is a one-line edit to a file nothing in the console will touch for you.

THE TARGET HAS CHANGED, AND THIS ENTRY SAYS SO RATHER THAN SWAPPING THE STRING QUIETLY. For seven weeks this read `anthropic/claude-opus-5`. Anthropic shipped claude-opus-5-5 on 2026-09-22 — the day AFTER the last run, which is why it was missed and not a judgement that was wrong — at $4/$20 per 1M against claude-opus-5's $5/$25. So last week's target is itself superseded, by something 20% cheaper on both sides of the meter. The alias is now 47 days outstanding (first raised 2026-08-19, from git) and the wired claude-opus-4-8 dates from 2026-05-28: three generations back, same tier, same alias. ONE THING IS WEAKER THAN LAST WEEK'S VERSION AND IS FLAGGED: claude-opus-5 had a parallel alias from the 2026-08-19 wire-all, so repointing was free. claude-opus-5-5 does NOT — the last sweep ran 2026-09-18, four days before it shipped — so it is reachable only once something adds it. The ai-router alias target is the vendor id either way, so the one-line edit still works on its own; but discovery should surface claude-opus-5-5 as newer-than-anything-wired on the next read, and a wire-all would pick it up.

TARGET CHANGED, same reason and same week as claude-opus. claude-sonnet-5-5 shipped 2026-09-28, seven days after the last run, at claude-sonnet-5's UNCHANGED $2/$10 per 1M — so unlike the opus repoint there is no price argument here at all, in either direction, and this entry should not manufacture one. The case is staleness and capability: the wired claude-sonnet-4-6 dates from 2026-02-17, which at 47 days outstanding makes this the oldest target in the file at seven and a half months, and Anthropic reports Sonnet 5.5 at 70.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 against Sonnet 5's 10.3% on agentic coding, which is the shape of work this box routes through the router. Like claude-opus-5-5 it post-dates the 2026-09-18 wire-all, so there is no parallel alias to lean on yet.

TARGET DELIBERATELY NOT MOVED, and the reasoning is the point of this entry. 47 days outstanding (first raised 2026-08-19, from git); the stable `gemini-flash` alias still fronts 3.6 while 3.7 is wired under its own id, so the repoint remains free. Google published gemini-3.8-flash on 2026-09-02 and now recommends it for new projects, which would normally move this target the way claude-opus moved. IT IS NOT BEING MOVED, on evidence from this repository: the console's own wire-all ran on 2026-09-18 — sixteen days after 3.8 Flash was published — and config/wired-models.json shows it added gemini-3.5-transcribe and nothing else from Google. Wire-all recomputes its candidate list server-side from this key's live ListModels, so the honest reading is that gemini-3.8-flash was not in this key's catalogue on 18 September, not that discovery missed it. This run had no GEMINI_API_KEY to re-check (see the note on vendor lists), so 3.7 stands and 3.8 is a thing to re-test after the next wire-all rather than a repoint to make blind. Still do NOT point this at gemini-flash-latest, which is also wired: a floating alias behind a stable alias is two moving parts where one was wanted.

Unchanged in every respect, and now 47 days outstanding — first raised 2026-08-19, dated from git, and the alias target in config/ai-router.yaml has not been touched since that date. gpt-transcribe appeared 2026-07-27, dropping the 4o generation marker the way gpt-image did; gpt-4o-transcribe dates from 2025-03. It is wired under its own id already, so this is the cheapest of the five. Note gemini-3.5-transcribe joined the router on 2026-09-18, which gives the audio_transcription mode a second vendor it did not have in August — useful context for whoever makes this edit, not a reason to point this alias anywhere but at OpenAI's current model.

notes: WHAT CHANGED SINCE THE LAST RUN: NOTHING WAS ADOPTED, and that is a mechanical finding rather than a memory. config/model-meta.json last changed on 2026-09-20, before the 21-09 report, so no candidate's checkpoint has appeared there. All five alias targets in `upgrades` were last touched in config/ai-router.yaml on 2026-08-19 — checked with `git log -1 -S<target>` per target, not by reading the file — so none of the five repoints has been made. BeTenshi still serves stt from whisper-large-v3 on :8001, tts from Kokoro on :8002 with Chatterbox on :8004, and image from Qwen-Image on :8021. The only config change touching this report's subject matter since 21-09 is config/hosts/b5.json moving B5's image driver from the Draw Things CLI to mflux, which is a runtime fix and not an adoption. Ages in this file are all read from `git log --follow config/model-scout.json`: cohere-transcribe 2026-08-24 (42 days), qwen3-tts 2026-08-24 (42), vibevoice-asr-streaming 2026-09-07 (28), gpt-5.5 2026-09-07 (28), the other four upgrades 2026-08-19 (47).

DROPPED THIS WEEK: `qwen3-asr-1.7b-hf`, on judgement rather than on the adoption rule, so the reason is given in full. Its checkpoint is not in config/model-meta.json, so rule 1b did not force it out; B5 serves a different build (`qwen3-asr-1.7b-8bit`, MLX) and BeTenshi serves neither. It is dropped because the one lane now had three entries for one slot, which is how this list stopped being selective the last time. ITS FACT SURVIVES WITHOUT THE ROW: Qwen3-ASR-1.7B is still open #1 of 52 on the 02-10-2026 short-form English board at 4.311 WER, and that is the best open short-form English number there is. What it cannot do is carry a recommendation: it is absent from the long-form board entirely, and on multilingual it is 5.115 against whisper-large-v3's 4.810 — WORSE than the model it would replace on BeTenshi. A candidate that wins one board, loses another to the incumbent and is unmeasured on the third is a data point, not advice, and the Leaderboard tab is where data points live. Cohere beats whisper on all three; parakeet matches the whisper-beating at a fifth of the VRAM. Between those two there was nothing left for this entry to say.

THE STT RANKING, from the Open ASR Leaderboard build dated 02-10-2026 — the build id and the source revisions are listed in the Space's init.py under VERSIONS, and the files pulled were hf-audio/open-asr-leaderboard-results/english_short_latest.csv (rev c23ca4f), hf-audio/leaderboard_longform/longform_latest.csv (rev 4f164c2) and hf-audio/multilingual_evals/multilingual_latest.csv. The build's own label: 'Add TheStageAI/thewhisper-large-v3-turbo, add FermionResearch/Phonon-2, update ibm-granite/granite-speech-5.0 with speed-up. Add Armenian to multilingual.' 52 of the 66 short-form rows are open-weights. OPEN SHORT-FORM ENGLISH, average WER, lower better: Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-hf 4.311, Hojo-ASR-V1 4.334, higgs-audio-v3-stt 4.393, canary-qwen-2.5b 4.428, ARK-ASR-3B 4.475, thewhisper-large-v3-turbo 4.539, ARK-ASR-0.6B 4.559, granite-speech-4.1-2b 4.615, MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 4.636, cohere-transcribe 4.670 (#10), parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 4.859 (#16), Phonon-2 5.169 (#24), nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b 5.245 (#25), VibeVoice-ASR-HF 5.575 (#32), whisper-large-v3 5.780 (#35 of 52). LONG-FORM, average: cohere 9.733, parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 10.720, whisper-large-v3-turbo 11.010, canary-qwen-2.5b 11.203, whisper-large-v3 11.228. MULTILINGUAL, average over fourteen language/dataset pairs: cohere 3.830, Voxtral-Small-24B 3.697, whisper-large-v3 4.810, parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 4.814, Qwen3-ASR-1.7B 5.115, whisper-large-v3-turbo 5.557. THE CROSS-JOIN IS THE FINDING, and it was computed rather than eyeballed: only four open models appear on all three boards — cohere, parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3, whisper-large-v3 and whisper-large-v3-turbo — and only cohere beats whisper-large-v3 on every one. Models that look like they qualify and do not: canary-qwen-2.5b and Voxtral-Small-24B are absent from multilingual and long-form respectively; Qwen3-ASR and Hojo-ASR-V1 are absent from long-form. A model absent from a board is unmeasured there, not average there.

TWO MEASURED STREAMING ASR MODELS THAT THE LICENCE RULE KEEPS OUT OF `candidates`, recorded here so the next run does not rediscover them. nvidia/nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b: 5.245 short-form English (better than whisper-large-v3's 5.780), RTFx 1,167, cache-aware FastConformer with an RNN-T head, model.safetensors 2,472,413,604 B plus a q8_0 GGUF at 699,872,960 B — but `license: other`, specifically the nvidia-open-model-license. nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b: 7.878 across 40 declared languages, RTFx 1,345, under OpenMDW-1.1. Neither is a standard open licence and neither is a click-through over known terms, so under this file's own rule they wait in notes until a person has read them. If someone does read the NVIDIA open model licence and finds it acceptable, the first of these is the strongest streaming option on the board and would displace the VibeVoice candidate outright: it is measured, it beats the incumbent, and it is 0.70 GB as a GGUF.

THE OPEN TTS LEADERBOARD HAS GONE DARK, AND BOTH TTS ENTRIES ABOVE DEPEND ON IT. Clause 2c of the brief says to rank text-to-speech on hf-audio/open_tts_leaderboard and cite the build pulled. The Space is still there and its code is still readable — leaderboard_data.py names the current build as 30-09-2026 ('Add Photon engine for streaming (Qwen3TTS and Kokoro)') — but the results themselves live in hf-audio/tts_leaderboard_results, which now returns HTTP 401 to an anonymous request and is invisible to this run's authenticated hub account. It was readable on 18-09, which is where every TTS number in this file comes from. TWO CONSEQUENCES, both of which a reader needs. FIRST, nothing in the TTS lane was re-verified this week; the 18-09 figures are carried forward and labelled as such in each entry rather than restated as current. SECOND, AND WORSE: the registry labels the 29-09 build 'Sync results programmatically (few instances of bad manual copies from initial version)', which is the maintainers saying some numbers from the builds this report quoted were mis-transcribed by hand. A published Pareto chart from the board's author, dated after that sync, puts OmniVoice at 3.25, Qwen3-TTS-12Hz at 4.11 and VoxCPM2 at 4.36 where the 18-09 CSVs gave 3.39, 4.22 and 4.45 — the same ordering, all three slightly lower. That is consistent with a re-sync rather than a reshuffle, and it is NOT treated here as a reading of the board: it is a chart, the dataset and language selection behind it cannot be checked, and reading values off a picture is not the same as pulling a CSV. It is reported only as evidence that the numbers moved. Until the dataset is readable again, clause 5b's fallback does not apply either — the board exists, it is simply shut, which is a different situation from a capability that has no benchmark.

THE TTS SHORTLIST CLAUSE 2c ASKED THIS RUN TO EVALUATE, answered rather than deferred. ResembleAI/chatterbox: already shipped, running on BeTenshi as the `voice` service on :8004 since 18-09, so it is settled. ResembleAI/chatterbox-turbo (MIT, English): RULED OUT, and not for lack of data. It ships real weights — t3_turbo_v1.safetensors 1,915,480,052 B, s3gen 1,056,484,620 B, s3gen_meanflow 1,064,875,036 B, 4.04 GB in total — but it is English-only, and English is precisely where BeTenshi is already well served: Kokoro is 82M, second on the 18-09 English board at 1.46 WER, and the fastest thing near the top at 103.9 ms to first audio. A 4 GB English-only model has nothing to take from an 82M one. Worth recording for whoever looks next: the hub reports 0 downloads for this repo on BOTH metrics — 0 over 30 days and 0 all-time — against 696 likes, which is a broken counter rather than evidence of zero adoption, and means this repo cannot be ranked on adoption even if clause 5b's fallback were available. YatharthS/LuxTTS (apache-2.0, ONNX, English): RULED OUT for the same reason, more easily. It is small — fm_decoder.onnx 477,534,010 B with an int8 build at 124,657,100 B, text_encoder 17,633,735 B, vocos 63,972,079 B, so roughly 559 MB at fp32 or 194 MB at int8 — and 55,368 all-time / 5,906 30-day downloads. Small and clean-licensed, but again English-only against an incumbent that is 82M and measured second on English. Neither model adds a capability either box lacks, so neither becomes a candidate. That is a verdict on what is already running, not a complaint about missing data.

THE IMAGE LANE IS STILL EMPTY, AND QWEN-IMAGE-2.1 IS THE REASON TO SAY SO EXPLICITLY. Trending text-to-image on the hub this week is Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1 (published 2026-09-30) and roughly a dozen derivatives of it — GGUF conversions, turbo LoRAs, ControlNets. BeTenshi runs Qwen/Qwen-Image, which is apache-2.0, and a reader could reasonably assume the newer sibling is a drop-in upgrade. IT IS NOT, ON TWO COUNTS, both read off the repo rather than inferred. Its LICENSE file is the Qwen RESEARCH LICENSE AGREEMENT, release date 2026-09-20, which grants rights 'FOR NON-COMMERCIAL PURPOSES ONLY' and requires a separate commercial licence — so under this file's licence rule it cannot be a candidate, and every derivative inherits it (abenzerps, unsloth, Viggle, Pruna, Noctaluna GGUF/LoRA repos all carry `license: other` from the same base). And it is BIGGER, not smaller: 33,115,613,408 B of weights in the current revision — a 7.1B transformer (14,230,284,408 B) plus an 8.8B bf16 text encoder (17,534,339,488 B) plus a 1.35 GB VAE — against the 20.4B denoiser already installed. The 7.1B in the parameter field is the transformer alone and is the number that would mislead. On BeTenshi, where host RAM is the tighter constraint and Qwen-Image's 28 GB of standing offload has already killed a service, a 33 GB download under a non-commercial licence is a clear no. On B5's 128 GB unified pool the size would be survivable and the licence still is not. Clean-licensed alternatives were looked at and none beats what is installed: inclusionAI/Ming-Image-0.1-Design (MIT, graphic design and text rendering) reports 0 downloads and ships a custom loader, and SupraLabs/Supra2-IMG (apache-2.0, trained from scratch) has 878. Per clause 5b there is no public image benchmark to rank on, so that is adoption and licence talking, and neither has the adoption. BeTenshi keeps Z-Image-Turbo and Qwen-Image; B5 keeps FLUX.2 Klein.

VENDOR LISTS WERE NOT READ LIVE THIS WEEK, AND THE CLOUD HALF IS SOURCED ACCORDINGLY. This environment has no OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY, so step 3's live /models endpoints were unavailable and discovery could not be consulted from here. Everything in `upgrades` was therefore verified against each vendor's own published pages and dated: OpenAI's developer pricing page for the gpt-5.5 / 5.6 table and the 272K short/long-context split; Anthropic's published model catalogue for claude-opus-5-5 ($4/$20, 2026-09-22) and claude-sonnet-5-5 ($2/$10, 2026-09-28); Google's Gemini deprecation page for the retirement dates below. Where a claim needed the live catalogue and could not get it — specifically whether gemini-3.8-flash is offered to this key — the entry says so and declines to move rather than guessing. The console's own discovery, which does read the live lists, will answer that on the next read and is the right place for it.

A WIRED ALIAS HAS LIKELY GONE DEAD, which is the failure mode this whole tab exists to prevent. Google's deprecation page gives gemini-2.5-flash-image a shutdown date of 2026-10-02 — three days ago — with gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview named as the replacement. config/wired-models.json carries `gemini-2.5-flash-image` -> `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-image`, added by the wire-all on 2026-09-18, two weeks after Google had already published the date. THE DAMAGE IS SMALL AND THE SHAPE IS NOT: nothing routes through that alias — the stable image aliases are `gemini-image` (gemini-3-pro-image) and `gemini-image-fast` (gemini-3.1-flash-image), and the latter is already the recommended replacement — so this is one dead row in the managed block rather than a broken route. But it is the first time discovery has left something behind that it has no way to clean up: wire-all adds, and there is no unwire path, so a model the vendor retires stays in config/wired-models.json until someone edits it by hand. Also on that page and worth a diary entry rather than an action: gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts and gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts, both wired, have no announced shutdown date but are superseded by gemini-3.8-flash-tts; and Google says the 2.5 line stays available 'until further notice' for existing usage, so the alias may still answer. Verify before deleting anything — this is a note, not an instruction, and the alias is not in `upgrades` because it is console-managed rather than hand-written.
